name: abort
doc: This cancels execution of a program script and returns control to the application. The database is not updated. The function has the same effect in both 3GL and 4GL scripts.
syntax: function void abort ()

name: abort.io
doc: This cancels the current database transaction.
syntax: function void abort.io (string mesg(14) [, ...])

name: abort.transaction
doc: This cancels the current database transaction. No changes are stored in the database.
syntax: function long abort.transaction ()

name: abs
doc: This function returns the absolute value of the supplied numeric value.
syntax: function double abs (void value)
returns: If the type of the input value is not double, then implicit type conversion of the input value to type long is performed. Then, if the resulting value (of type double or of type long) is negative, th…

name: acos
doc: This computes the arc cosine of x. The value of x must be in the range [-1, 1].
syntax: function double acos (double x)
returns: The arc cosine of x, expressed as a floating point number in the range [0, p] radians.

syntax: function boolean compnr.check (long new_compnr)

name: compress.pixmap
doc: This converts a specified colormap and pixmap to a picture in .gif format.
syntax: function long compress.pixmap (long colormap, long num_colors, string pixmap(), long width, long height, ref string buffer, ref long buffer_length)
returns: TRUE (<> 0): success FALSE (0): error

name: concat$
doc: The function concat$ converts one or more values to strings and concatenates them, separated by a separator, to a single string. You can use string.scan() to split the string again into its individual parts.
syntax: function string concat$ (string separator, void value ...)
returns: The return value is the concatenation of the supplied values (implicitly converted to string values), separated by the specified separator character. As of bshell TIV level 2340, the resulting string…

name: copy.cdf
doc: This function facilitates the application in the task of carrying forward the information in the CDFs through the business process. The function will copy CDFs from a source record buffer to a destination record buffer if the destination table has a CDF with the same name.
syntax: function long copy.cdf (long dest.table.id, long src.table.id)

name: copy.image
doc: This function will copy an image or set of images based on its guid into then image repository refered by the target guid. This function can be used when copying records.
syntax: function long copy.image (string source.guid, string source.tablename, string target.guid, string target.tablename [, boolean overwrite])

name: copy.image.to.company
doc: This function will copy an image or set of images based on its guid into the image repository referred to by the target guid and company. This function can be used when copying records to a different company.
syntax: function long copy.image.to.company (long source.company, string source.guid, string source.tablename, long target.company, string target.guid, string target.tablename [, boolean overwrite] [, boolean omit.transaction])

name: copy.image.to.file
doc: This function will copy an image based on its company, guid, and table into a file.
syntax: function long copy.image.to.file (long source.company, string source.guid, string source.tablename, string target.file)

name: copy.mem
doc: This copies the memory space from the source argument to the destination argument. By default, the total length of source is copied. But, if the destination argument is shorter than the source argument, then source is truncated. Use the optional count argument to copy a specified number of array el…
syntax: function void copy.mem (ref void destination, void source [, long count])

name: cos
doc: This computes the cosine of x, in radians. The x argument can be a long or a double.
syntax: function double cos (double x)
returns: The cosine of x.

name: cosh
doc: This computes the hyperbolic cosine of x.
syntax: function double cosh (double x)
returns: The hyperbolic cosine of x.

name: count.records.in.view
doc: Counts the number of records that exist in the maintable for the current view. Any filter or query extension that has been set is taken into account.
syntax: function long count.records.in.view ()
returns: The number of records that are exists in the maintable for the current view.

name: cps.add.child
doc: Add a child session to this controller, which will be shown and started in the frame of the composite controller. This session will be shown in the passed split pane. To a split pane exactly two objects must be added: sessions and/or split panes. The order of adding these objects to the split pane…
syntax: function long cps.add.child (const string session.code, long bars, const string title, long splitpane)

name: cps.add.tree.detail.session
doc: Add a Tree-Detail session to detail area. Standard the detail session of cps.set.tree.detail is shown. The added tree detail can be activated with the function gbf.synchronize.detail(). Maximum of 4 Sessions can be added.
syntax: function long cps.add.tree.detail.session (const string detail.session.code)

name: cps.create.splitpane
doc: Create a split pane which can either hold another split pane or a child session. There can only be one top-level split pane created. This function may not be called before the call to cps.init()
syntax: function long cps.create.splitpane (long orientation, long divider [, long splitpane])

name: cps.init
doc: Initialize the Composite Session Controller. This must be the first cps function called by the 3GL-Script. When this session was started from a parent session in modeless mode, this function will reactive the parent session. So any imports which must be done by this session from the parent should b…
syntax: function long cps.init ( [long cps.type])

name: cps.set.tree.detail
doc: Sets the GBF session and Details sesion of a Tree-Detail session. The GBF session and Details session will be shown and started in the frame of the composite controller.
syntax: function long cps.set.tree.detail (const string tree.session.code, const string detail.session.code [, long divider] [, const string tree.title])

name: cps.start
doc: Activates the Composite Session Controller and the related child sessions. This function will only return when the user decides to close this composite session.
syntax: function void cps.start ()

name: cps.status.mess
doc: This function displays the specified message in the status bar of a composite session. To clear this message, an empty message string must be passed. This function can be called from composite child sessions (GBF or 4GL). When this function is called from other session types, it will do nothing.
syntax: function void cps.status.mess (const string message)

returns: The name of the temporary file.

returns: > 0 success 0 toolbar not allowed in this type of session -1 incorrect number of arguments

syntax: function long create.keyfields.collection ()

name: create.local.directory

name: create.progress.indicator
doc: This creates a progress indicator with the specified title displayed in its title bar. The progress indicator is activated after the first update (using change.progress.indicator()). It is removed again using destroy.progress.indicator(), or automatically if PROGRESS.NOAUTODESTROY is not specified.

returns: curl.strerror$()

name: dal.any.parent.changed
doc: The function dal.any.parent.changed() determines whether any of the fields, from which the current field depends, is changed. This function can only be used in combination with dal.require.field().
syntax: function boolean dal.any.parent.changed ()
returns: true one or more parent fields have changed false no parent field has changed

name: dal.change.object
doc: Use this to indicate the DAL that the current record is about to be changed. After this call, fields can be changed with dal.set.field(). And after that, the record can be saved with dal.save.object().

name: dal.check.field

syntax: function long dal.check.field (string fld.name [, long element] [, long mode])

name: dal.clear.error.messages
doc: This clears all DAL error messages from the message buffer. Abbreviation for dal.reset.error.messages(0).
syntax: function void dal.clear.error.messages ()

name: dal.clear.messages
doc: This clears all DAL messages of the specified type from the message buffer. Abbreviation for dal.reset.messages(i.type, 0).
syntax: function void dal.clear.messages (long i.type)

name: dal.copy.object
doc: Use this to indicate the DAL that a record is about to be copied. In contrary to dal.new.object(), this function does not call the set.object.defaults() hook!

name: dal.count.error.messages
doc: MSG.ERROR

syntax: function long dal.count.messages (long i.type)
returns: The number of DAL messages of the specified type.

name: dal.destroy
doc: Use this to delete a database record. The function encapsulates the db.delete() function with the DAL hooks of the object set. If the before.destroy.object() hook fails, the database operation is cancelled.
syntax: function void dal.destroy (string dal.name, long object_set, ref long retval, long prop_check [, long mode] [, long eflag])

name: dal.destroy.object
doc: Deletes a record of the given table. The record must have been locked for update. This function does the same as dal.destroy(), however it does more detailed permission checking. Further, the method.is.allowed() hook is always called ( dal.destroy() allows you to skip this hook by passing FALSE to…
syntax: function long dal.destroy.object (string tbl.name [, long error.flag])

name: dal.get.property.flag

returns: The function returns the value of the has_changed flag of the specified property. The possible values are: Properties with no check function in the DAL always return 0.

returns: TRUE in case the field has changed, FALSE in case the field has not changed.

syntax: function long dal.save.object (string tbl.name [, long error.flag])

name: dal.set.array.field

name: date.to.date
doc: This converts a date and time in one time zone to the corresponding date and time in a different time zone.
syntax: function long date.to.date (long in_date, long in_time, const string in_zone, const string out_zone, ref long out_date, ref long out_time)

name: date.to.inputstr$
doc: This converts a specified number of days since 01-01-0001 to a date input string.
syntax: function string date.to.inputstr$ (long dayno, string format(7), long length)

name: date.to.iso
doc: This converts a local date to an ISO 8601 date string. This is a string with the format: yyyy-mm-dd
syntax: function string date.to.iso (long local.date)
returns: The string representation of the local date in ISO 8601 format. If an invalid local date is specified, the following string is returned: "0000-00-00"

name: date.to.num
doc: This returns the number of days since 01-01-0001 for a specified year, month, and day of the month.
syntax: function long date.to.num (long yearno, long monthno, long month_dayno)

name: date.to.utc
doc: This converts the specified local date and time to UTC long format. Input values must be in the signed 32-bit value range.
syntax: function domain ttutc date.to.utc (long yearno, long monthno, long month_dayno, long hours, long minutes, long seconds)

name: date.with.timezone.info.to.utc
doc: This converts the specified local date and time to UTC long format. For this conversion it will NOT use the timezone of the user, but the difference in seconds to UTC as supplied in the variable utcdiff. Input values must be in the signed 32-bit value range.
syntax: function domain ttutc date.with.timezone.info.to.utc (long yearno, long monthno, long month_dayno, long hours, long minutes, long seconds, long utcdiff)

name: db.bind
doc: This creates a pointer to a specified table. It returns a table ID that you use in other database calls to identify the table. The pointer is to a table with a particular company number and record buffer. You can create additional pointers to the same table by calling the function with a different…

name: db.blob.append

doc: This function appends data from an XML tree to the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers. Before calling db.blob.append.xml(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database.
syntax: function long db.blob.append.xml (const string blob.locator, long xml.node [, long mode] [, long eflag])

name: db.blob.clear
doc: This function clears the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers. Before calling db.blob.clear(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database.
syntax: function long db.blob.clear (const string blob.locator [, long mode] [, long eflag])

doc: This function reads data from the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers. Before calling db.blob.read(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. syntax: function long db.blob.read (const string blob.locator, long offset, long num.bytes, ref string bytes.array, ref long num.bytes.read)

name: db.blob.read.xml
doc: This function reads data from the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers, and parses it to an XML tree. Before calling db.blob.read.xml(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. For example, the following code retrieves the BLOB locator that refers to a certain picture from a table, and t…
syntax: function long db.blob.read.xml (const string blob.locator, long offset, ref long bytes.read, ref long xml.node, ref string error, long whitespacehandling)

name: db.blob.read.xml.ns
doc: This function reads data from the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers, and parses it to an XML tree. Before calling db.blob.read.xml.ns(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. For example, the following code retrieves the BLOB locator that refers to a certain picture from a table, an…
syntax: function long db.blob.read.xml.ns (const string blob.locator, long offset, ref long bytes.read, ref long xml.node, ref string error, long whitespacehandling)

name: db.blob.size
doc: This function retrieves the size of the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers. Before calling db.blob.size(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. For example, the following code retrieves the BLOB locator that refers to a certain picture from a table, and then retrieves the size of th…
syntax: function long db.blob.size (const string blob.locator, ref long num.bytes)

name: db.change.order
doc: This makes a specified index the current index. After this action, the record pointer is undefined.
syntax: function long db.change.order (long table_id, long index_nr [, long compnr])

name: db.check.restricted
doc: In a table definition, it is possible to set restrictions on update and/or delete actions for records that are referenced by other tables. These restrictions mean that you cannot delete and/or update the primary key that is referenced by another table. This function checks whether there are referen…
syntax: function long db.check.restricted (long table_id, long mode, ref string message(256))

name: db.check.row.changed
doc: This function checks whether a record that has been delayed locked and changed by the current process has been changed by another process ("user"). It does not check whether the row has been modified in the current process. In a way it answers the question: "If I would update the current record now…
syntax: function long db.check.row.changed (long table_id)

name: db.check.row.dlocked
doc: This checks whether the row, identified by its primary key columns is delayed locked or not. If the row is already locked, the function returns the dlock number of the row. This function can result in a considerable performance gain as it eradicates the need for multiple reads of the same record.
syntax: function long db.check.row.dlocked (long table_id)

name: db.check.row.domains
doc: This checks whether the current record of a specified table conforms to the domain definitions in the data dictionary. All fields of the record are checked in turn until an error occurs. The function returns when the first error is encountered.
syntax: function long db.check.row.domains (long table_id, ref string fld_name)
returns: If an error is returned, you can retrieve information about the specific error using db.error.message().

name: db.clear.table
doc: This deletes all data from a specified table. Reference counters are automatically updated.
syntax: function long db.clear.table (long table_id [, long flag] [, long comp_nr])
returns: 0: success <> 0: error

name: db.columns.to.record
doc: The record buffer of a table is used for reading records from, or writing records to, that table. When you bind to a table (see db.bind()) and specify that the default record buffer is to be used, the contents of the table fields are automatically copied to the buffer. This does not happen when you…
syntax: function long db.columns.to.record (long table_id)

name: db.create.table
doc: This creates a new database table.
syntax: function long db.create.table (long table_id, long compnr)

name: db.curr
doc: This reads the current record from a specified table.
syntax: function long db.curr (long table_id [, long lock])

name: db.delete
doc: This deletes the current record. The record pointer is not changed, so the current record is undefined after the record has been deleted.
syntax: function long db.delete (long table_id [, long mode] [, long eflag])

name: db.drop.table
doc: This deletes a specified table. Data and indices associated with the table are also deleted. Reference counters are automatically updated.
syntax: function long db.drop.table (long table_id [, long flag] [, long comp_nr])

name: db.eq
doc: This reads from a specified table the record whose key value equals a certain predefined value. Before calling db.eq(), you must assign the required value to the key field. For example, the following code retrieves the item with item number 001 from the items table:
syntax: function long db.eq (long table_id [, long lock])

name: db.error
doc: Use this to retrieve the error code returned by the most recent database action. If you specify a table ID, the function retrieves the most recent error code returned by an action on that table.
syntax: function long db.error ( [long table_id])

name: db.error.message
doc: Some errors returned by a database action have an associated error message. This message provides additional information about the error. Use the db.error.message() function to retrieve the error message (if any) associated with the most recent error code returned by a database action.
syntax: function string db.error.message ()
returns: The error message associated with the most recent error that occurred. Or an empty string if no message is associated with the error.

name: db.first
doc: This reads the first record from a specified table. It uses the current index to search the table.
syntax: function long db.first (long table_id [, long lock])

name: db.flush
doc: All buffered actions are flushed to the database.
syntax: function long db.flush ()

name: db.ge
doc: This reads from a specified table the record whose key value is greater than or equal to a certain predefined value. Before calling db.ge(), you must assign the required value to the key field. For example:
syntax: function long db.ge (long table_id [, long lock])

name: db.get.error.bypass
doc: This function returns the current value of error.bypass and, optionally, the current value of error.bypass.with.retry. It is allowed to call this function without having called the db.set.error.bypass.on() function.
syntax: function boolean db.get.error.bypass ( [ref boolean with.retry])
returns: The current value of error.bypass.

name: db.get.physical.compnr
doc: Use this to retrieve the physical company number for the specified table ( tblname) and logical company number ( logical.compnr).
syntax: function long db.get.physical.compnr (string tblname, long logical.compnr)

name: db.gt
doc: This reads from a specified table the record whose key value is greater than a certain predefined value. Before calling db.gt(), you must assign the required value to the key field. For example:

syntax: function long db.indexinfo (long table_id, long index_nr, ref long index_info(32, 3), ref long indexparts, ref boolean indexdups, ref boolean indexactive)

name: db.insert
doc: This adds a new record to a specified table. The record pointer does not change.
syntax: function long db.insert (long table_id [, long mode] [, long eflag])

name: db.last
doc: This reads the last record from a specified table. It uses the current index to search the table.
syntax: function long db.last (long table_id [, long lock])

name: db.le
doc: This reads from a specified table the record whose key value is less than or equal to a certain predefined value. Before calling db.le(), you must assign the required value to the key field. For example:
syntax: function long db.le (long table_id [, long lock])

name: db.lock.table
doc: This locks a specified table. Other users cannot then write to or delete the table or any parts of the table. Nor can they lock the table or any parts of the table. The lock is released by commit.transaction() or abort.transaction()
syntax: function long db.lock.table (long table_id)

name: db.lt
doc: This reads from a specified table the record whose key value is less than a certain predefined value. Before calling db.lt(), you must assign the required value to the key field. For example:
syntax: function long db.lt (long table_id [, long lock])

name: db.max.retry
doc: This function returns the value of the MAX_RETRY resource setting, which indicates how often the system may return to a retry point as a result of an abort in an update action.
syntax: function long db.max.retry ()
returns: The value of the MAX_RETRY resource.

name: db.next
doc: This reads the next record from a specified table. It uses the current index to search the table. If there is no current record, the function returns an error message.
syntax: function long db.next (long table_id [, long lock])

name: db.nr.indices
doc: This returns the number of indices that exist on a specified table.
syntax: function long db.nr.indices (long table_id, ref long nr_indices)

name: db.nr.rows
doc: This returns the number of rows that a specified table contains.
syntax: function long db.nr.rows (long table_id, ref long nr_rows [, long comp_nr])

name: db.permission
doc: Use this to check the access permissions that a user has to a specified table or table field.
syntax: function long db.permission (long table_id, string field [, ref string buffer])
returns: The function returns a long that indicates the permissions that the user has on the table or on a specified field of that table. The return value consists of one of, or a combination of, the followin…

name: db.prev
doc: This reads the previous record from a specified table. It uses the current index to search the table. If there is no current record, the function returns an error message.
syntax: function long db.prev (long table_id [, long lock])

name: db.record.changed
doc: Tests whether the current value of the record buffer belonging to the given table id has changed since the last call of db.store.record().
syntax: function boolean db.record.changed (long table_id [, long size])

name: db.record.to.columns
doc: When you bind to a table (see db.bind() and specify that the default record buffer is to be used, the contents of the buffer are automatically copied to the table fields in your program script. This does not happen when you specify a record buffer other than the default buffer.
syntax: function long db.record.to.columns (long table_id)

name: db.ref.handle.mode
doc: Use this to check whether a full table scan (FTS) is necessary during delete or update operations. Delete and update operations can take a long time to complete when the table is referenced by other tables but no reference counter is kept (cascade, nullify, or lookup mode). When there is no index o…
syntax: function long db.ref.handle.mode (string table_name, long mode)

name: db.restore.record
doc: This restores the record of the given table that was stored previously with db.store.record(). Also the table's field values will be restored.
syntax: function void db.restore.record (long table_id)

name: db.retry.hit
doc: Use this to check whether the client database layer has returned to a retry point. You must set the retry point by using db.retry.point() before you call db.retry.hit(). See also Database handling overview.
syntax: function long db.retry.hit ()

name: db.retry.point
doc: This sets a retry point for the current transaction. The program returns to this point if an error occurs during the transaction; the transaction is then retried. When you include a retry point for a transaction, you must set it before the start of the transaction.
syntax: function void db.retry.point ()

name: db.row.length
doc: Use this to retrieve the length of records in a specified table.
syntax: function long db.row.length (long table_id, ref long row_length)

name: db.set.error.bypass.off
doc: This function resets the values of error.bypass and error.bypass.with.retry to the previous values. The function must be called exactly once for each time the function db.set.error.bypass.on() is called. Calling this function more often than calling db.set.error.bypass.on() is a programming error a…
syntax: function void db.set.error.bypass.off ()

name: db.set.error.bypass.on
doc: This function flushes all buffered database actions in the current transaction before setting the error.bypass and error.bypass.with.retry flags. If any of the database actions results in a retryable error a jump is made to the db.retry.point(). If any of the actions results in a fatal error, then…
syntax: function long db.set.error.bypass.on ( [boolean with.retry])

name: db.set.to.default
doc: This sets bound variables in the program script to the default values defined in the data dictionary.
syntax: function long db.set.to.default (long table_id)

name: db.store.record
doc: Creates a copy of the current value of the record buffer belonging to the given table id. Later on this copied value can be restored by calling db.restore.record().
syntax: function void db.store.record (long table_id [, long size])

name: db.unbind
doc: This deletes the specified table pointer.
syntax: function long db.unbind (long table_id)

name: db.update
doc: This rewrites the current record. When updating a record with this function, you are permitted to update the primary key of the record.
syntax: function long db.update (long table_id [, long mode] [, long eflag])

name: dbcm.checked.out.objects.present

returns: ENOREC Another database error.

doc: Retrieves the Change Management status of the Object that is identified by the given Typed Object Id.

returns: DBCM_STATUS_DRAFT DBCM_STATUS_DRAFT_REV DBCM_STATUS_PENDING DBCM_STATUS_RECALL_REQ DBCM_STATUS_REJECTED DBCM_STATUS_APPR_RECVD DBCM_STATUS_APPROVED

returns: The functional id as string (key parts are concatenated using commas); or an empty string in case of an error.

doc: Returns the currently selected object action (as selected with dbcm.select.object.action()), or an empty string in case no object action has been selected.
syntax: function string dbcm.get.object.action$ ()
returns: The currently selected object action, or an empty string in case no object action is set.

name: dbcm.get.object.id$
doc: Returns the id of the currently selected object instance (as selected with dbcm.select.object.instance()), or an empty string in case no object instance is selected or if a previously selected object instance is out of scope.
syntax: function string dbcm.get.object.id$ ()
returns: The id of the currently selected object instance, or an empty string in case no object instance is set.

name: dbcm.get.object.type$
doc: Returns the currently selected object type (as selected with dbcm.select.object.type()), or an empty string in case no object type is selected or if the previously selected object type is out of scope.
syntax: function string dbcm.get.object.type$ ()
returns: The currently selected object type, or an empty string in case no object type is set.

doc: Retrieves the CM Action of the current record of the given table id.

returns: There is no checked-out version of this record. Note that this particular may still be part of a checked-out business object. Conceptually, the complete business object is checked-out, however on ind…

returns: The Typed Object ID, or an empty string in case no Typed Object ID could be found.

returns: The root table code, or an empty string in case of an error.

syntax: function long dbcm.get.type.name (const string tbl.name$, ref string obj.type$)

name: dbcm.get.user

syntax: function long dbcm.get.user (const string toid$, ref string user$)

name: dbcm.get.workflow.definition

name: dbcm.get.workflow.id

returns: DBCM_INVALID_STATE A database error occurred.

name: DsCbarMenu
doc: A DsCbarMenu object defines a menu bar and associated drop-down and cascaded menus. The menu bar is displayed across the top of a main window (DsCmwindow), below the title bar.

name: DsCcheckBox
doc: A check box represents a choice that has two states (selected or not selected). It appears as a square box with an accompanying label. When the choice is selected, a check mark appears in the box. When the choice is not selected, the box is empty.

name: DsCcolorCell
doc: A color cell is a rectangular child window that displays a color. If possible, a color cell uses only one palette entry and so saves resources. Otherwise, the number of colors used increases with every change.

name: DsCcolormap
doc: A color map defines an array of colors that can be used by a DsCpixmap object. The DsNdata attribute of a pixmap object contains an array of indexes into the color table of a DsCcolormap object.

name: DsCdrawnButton
doc: A DsCdrawnButton object has the same functionality as a DsCpushButton object except that it displays a graphical image instead of a text label.

name: DsCfield
doc: A DsCfield object provides a rectangular child window where the user can enter and edit text. It can be defined to support a single line or multiple lines of text. A DsCfield object provides the same functionality as a Windows text box (also referred to as an edit control).

name: DsCfontSet
doc: A DsCfontSet object defines a set of font attributes that other objects can apply to text strings. Objects indicate the font set to use by specifying the object ID of the font set in their DsNfontSet attribute.

name: DsCframe
doc: A DsCframe object places a three-dimensional border around a single child object.

name: DsCgc
doc: A graphical context object (DsCgc) defines a set of attributes that can be applied to graphical parts (that is, to subobjects of type DsCgpArc, DsCgpLine, DsCgpPie, and so on).

name: DsCgpArc
doc: A DsCgpArc object defines a circular or elliptical arc inside a rectangle. The center of the circle or ellipse is the center of the rectangle. The major and minor axes are specified by the width and height attributes respectively. The parent object is always a graphical window (DsCgwindow).

name: DsCgpComposite
doc: A DsCgpComposite subobject groups a number of graphical parts so that you can manipulate them as a single unit. The parent object is always a DsCgwindow object.

name: DsCgpGroupBox
doc: A DsCgpGroupBox object defines a frame on the parent window. It can also display a text string at the top of the frame. The parent object is always a DsCgwindow object.

name: DsCgpHeader
doc: A DsCgpHeader subobject defines a header line on the parent window. The line can include a centered title string. The parent window is always a DsCgwindow object.

name: DsCgpImage
doc: A DsCgpImage object defines a graphical image to be drawn in the parent window. It is linked to a DsCpixmap object, which defines an array of pixels, with a specified width, height, and depth (number of planes), but no screen coordinates. The parent window is always a DsCgwindow object.

name: DsCgpLine
doc: A DsCgpLine subobject defines a line to be drawn between two specified points in the parent window. The parent window is always a DsCgwindow object.

name: DsCgpOleSite
doc: A DsCgpOleSite subobject defines a rectangle that can embed an OLE object. The parent window is always a DsCgwindow object.

name: DsCgpPie
doc: A DsCgpPie subobject defines a filled circular or elliptical arc, within a bounding rectangle. This subobject is similar to a DsCgpArc subobject, except that it is filled with a color and fill style. The parent object is always a graphical window (DsCgwindow).

name: DsCgpPolygon
doc: A DsCgpPolygon subobject defines a closed figure, bounded by three or more straight sides, which is drawn in the parent window. It is basically a polyline whose first and last points are joined. A polygon subobject can have a fill color and style. The parent window is always a DsCgwindow object.

name: DsCgpPolyline
doc: A DsCgpPolyline subobject defines a line to be drawn between a number of specified points in the parent window. The points are stored in the DsNpointArray attribute. If the first and last points coincide, the lines are joined according to the setting of the DsNgcJoinStyle attribute. The parent wind…

name: DsCgpRectangle
doc: A DsCgpRectangle subobject defines a rectangle within the parent window. The parent window is always a DsCgwindow object.

name: DsCgpText
doc: A DsCgpText subobject defines a text string to be drawn as a graphical part in the parent window. The parent window is always a DsCgwindow object.

name: DsCgraph
doc: A graph is a rectangular child window that displays a graph. The DsCgraph object is not part of the standard Infor Enterprise Server object library. It is a third-party OCX control. It can be controlled from 3GL scripts in the same way as standard objects. Several graphs can be displayed simultaneo…

name: DsCgrid
doc: A DsCgrid object is a rectangular child window that displays a spreadsheet grid. Cells in the grid can contain not only data but also controls such as text boxes, list boxes, and check boxes.

name: DsCgwindow
doc: A graphical window (DsCgwindow) is a window in which applications can draw graphical parts such as lines, rectangles, polygons, and so on. Graphical windows also support user interface controls such as buttons, edit controls, list boxes, and so on.

name: DsClabel
doc: A DsClabel object provides a text string for labeling other objects.

name: DsCmwindow
doc: A main window (DsCmwindow) acts as the frame window for applications. It is used for starting processes and for creating graphical and character windows. Typically, a main window contains a border, title bar, control menu box, sizing controls, menu bar, toolbar, status bar, work area, and scroll ba…

name: DsCpixmap
doc: A DsCpixmap object defines a graphical image. It consists of a two-dimensional array of pixels, with a specified width, height, and depth (number of planes), but no screen coordinates. A pixmap is a resource that is used by other objects that can display an image. Objects that can use a pixmap incl…

name: DsCpushButton
doc: A pushbutton, also referred to as a command button, represents an action that is carried out when the user selects the button. A pushbutton displays a text label.

name: DsCradioBox
doc: A DsCradioBox object is an instance of DsCrowColumn object that contains radio buttons (also referred to as option buttons).

name: DsCradioButton
doc: A radio button (also referred to as an option button) represents a single option within a set of mutually exclusive options. It is either set or not set. Within a group of radio buttons, only one option in the group can be set. Selecting one radio button automatically deselects all others in the gr…

name: DsCrowColumn
doc: A DsCrowColumn object is a container object that displays its children in rows and columns.

name: DsCscrollbar
doc: Scroll bars enable users to scroll data that is too large to fit in the viewing window. They can be either horizontal or vertical. A scroll bar consists of the following components:

name: DsCscrollWindow
doc: A DsCscrollWindow object provides a scrollable view of a child object. It supports a single child object only. Scroll bars enable users to view the data not currently visible in the window. Scroll bars are visible only when the child object is larger than the scroll window.

name: DsCslider
doc: A slider object is used to set a value in a continuous range of values (for example, volume or brightness). It consists of a scroll bar that represents the full range of values and a movable slider whose position represents the current value. It also includes labels that indicate the slider's curre…

name: DsCstatusBar
doc: A DsCstatusBar object provides a status bar that displays help and status information in a main window (DsCmwindow object). Each main window can include one DsCstatusBar object. The status bar is positioned at the bottom of the window. It occupies part of the client area of the window. When a statu…

name: DsCtabFrame
doc: A DsCtabFrame object provides a window with one or more form tabs. The tabs can be arranged in a single line or in multiple lines. When tabs are arranged on a single line, scroll buttons are added automatically if the window is not large enough to accommodate all the tabs.

name: DsCtemplate
doc: A DsCtemplate object defines a set of attributes that can be applied to other objects.

name: DsCtoolBar
doc: A DsCtoolBar object defines a toolbar for a main window (DsCmwindow). An application creates the entire toolbar with a single create.object() call. Subsequently, it can use change.object() toadd, remove, change, enable, and disable toolbar buttons.

name: DsCtree
doc: A DsCtree object defines a tree view control. Like any tree view control, it displays a list of items as an indented outline that reflects the hierarchical relationship between the items.

syntax: function string http.cookie.value (long cookie)
returns: the cookie value

name: http.cookiejar.add
doc: Adds an http.cookie object to an http.cookiejar object.
syntax: function void http.cookiejar.add (long cookiejar, long cookie)

name: http.cookiejar.delete
doc: Deletes an http.cookiejar object. All contained http.cookie objects are deleted as well.
syntax: function void http.cookiejar.delete (long cookiejar)

name: http.cookiejar.first
doc: Returns the first http.cookie object of an http.cookiejar. This can be used to iterate all cookies in the cookiejar.
syntax: function long http.cookiejar.first (long cookiejar)
returns: the first http.cookie object in the cookiejar, or 0 if the cookiejar is empty

name: http.cookiejar.load
doc: Fills an http.cookiejar object with the cookies stored in the specified file.
syntax: function long http.cookiejar.load (ref long cookiejar, const string file)

name: http.cookiejar.new
doc: Creates a new empty http.cookiejar object.
syntax: function long http.cookiejar.new ()
returns: a new http.cookiejar object

name: http.cookiejar.save
doc: Saves the contents of an http.cookiejar object in a file. The contents of this file is overwritten.
syntax: function long http.cookiejar.save (long cookiejar, const string file)

name: http.delete
doc: Sends a DELETE HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.delete (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.get
doc: Sends a GET HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.get (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.head
doc: Sends a HEAD HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.head (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.header.name
doc: Returns the HTTP header name of an http.header object.
syntax: function string http.header.name (long header)
returns: the HTTP header name, eg. "Content-Type"

name: http.header.next
doc: Returns an http.header object's next http.header object.
syntax: function long http.header.next (long header)
returns: the next http.header object, or 0 if there is no next http.header object

name: http.header.value
doc: Returns the HTTP header value of an http.header object.
syntax: function string header.value (long header)
returns: the HTTP header value, e.g. "application/json" (which is a possible value of the "Content-Type" HTTP header)

name: http.headerlist.add
doc: Adds a name-value HTTP header pair to an http.headerlist object.
syntax: function void http.headerlist.add (long headerlist, const string name, const string value)

name: http.headerlist.add_list
doc: Adds the contents of another http.headerlist to an http.headerlist object.
syntax: function void http.headerlist.add_list (long headerlist, long other_headerlist)

name: http.headerlist.delete
doc: Deletes an http.headerlist object. All contained http.header objects are deleted as well.
syntax: function void http.headerlist.delete (long headerlist)

name: http.headerlist.first
doc: Returns the first http.header object of an http.headerlist. This can be used to iterate all HTTP headers in the list.
syntax: function long http.headerlist.first (long headerlist)
returns: the first http.header object in the list, or 0 if the list is empty

name: http.headerlist.get
doc: Gets the HTTP header with the specified name from an http.headerlist object. The name is searched in a case-insensitive way. The HTTP header is returned as an http.header object.
syntax: function long http.headerlist.get (long headerlist, const string name)
returns: the (first) http.header object with the specified name, or 0 if no header with the specified name was found

name: http.headerlist.get_all
doc: Returns a new http.headerlist object containing http.header objects with the given name. As this is a new list, you have to take care of deleting it when it is no longer needed.
syntax: function long http.headerlist.get_all (long headerlist, const string name)
returns: an http.headerlist object containing http.header objects with the specified name, or 0 if the specified header name was not found

name: http.headerlist.new
doc: Constructs a new http.headerlist object. It is possible to initialize the http.headerlist object with HTTP header name-value pairs.
syntax: function long http.headerlist.new ( ...)
returns: a new http.headerlist object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.mimepart.delete
doc: Deletes an http.mimepart object. If the http.mimepart object is part of an http.mimepartlist object is it removed from the mimepart list as well.
syntax: function void http.mimepart.delete (long mimepart)

name: http.mimepart.new
doc: Constructs a new http.mimepart object. Use the attributes as specified below to configure the MIME part.
syntax: function long http.mimepart.new ( ...)
returns: a new http.mimepart object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.mimepartlist.add
doc: Adds an http.mimepart object to an http.mimepartlist object.
syntax: function void http.mimepartlist.add (long mimepartlist, long http.mimepart)

name: http.mimepartlist.add_list
doc: Adds the contents of another http.mimepartlist to an http.mimepartlist object.
syntax: function void http.mimepartlist.add_list (long mimepartlist, long other_mimepartlist)

name: http.mimepartlist.delete
doc: Deletes an http.mimepartlist object. All contained http.mimepart objects are deleted as well.
syntax: function void http.mimepartlist.delete (long http.mimepartlist)

name: http.mimepartlist.new
doc: Constructs a new http.mimepartlist object.
syntax: function long http.mimepartlist.new ()
returns: a new http.mimepartlist object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.oauth1params.delete
doc: Deletes an http.oauth1params object.
syntax: function void http.oauth1params.delete (long oauth1params)

name: http.oauth1params.new
doc: Constructs a new http.oauth1params object. Use the attributes as specified below to specify the OAuth1 parameters.
syntax: function long http.oauth1params.new ( ...)
returns: a new http.oauth1params object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.options
doc: Sends an OPTIONS HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.options (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.patch
doc: Sends a PATCH HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.patch (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.post
doc: Sends a POST HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.post (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.put
doc: Sends a PUT HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.put (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.queryparamlist.add
doc: Adds a name-value query parameter pair to an http.queryparamlist object.
syntax: function void http.queryparamlist.add (long queryparamlist, const string name, const string value)

name: http.queryparamlist.add_list
doc: Adds the contents of another http.queryparamlist to an http.queryparamlist object.
syntax: function void http.queryparamlist.add_list (long queryparamlist, long other_queryparamlist)

name: http.queryparamlist.delete
doc: Deletes an http.queryparamlist object. Any contained name-value query parameter pairs are deleted as well.
syntax: function void http.queryparamlist.delete (long queryparamlist)

name: http.queryparamlist.new
doc: Constructs a new http.queryparamlist object. It is possible to initialize the http.queryparamlist object with name-value query parameter pairs. When the http.queryparamlist object is passed to eg. http.get(), the name and value pairs will be used to build a url-encoded querystring. The querystring…
syntax: function long http.queryparamlist.new ( ...)
returns: a new http.queryparamlist object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.queryparamlist.to_string
doc: Converts the key-value pairs in an http.queryparamlist object to an application/x-www-form-urlencoded string. The string can be used as the body of an HTTP request to post form data.
syntax: function string http.queryparamlist.to_string (long queryparamlist [, string sep(1)])
returns: an application/x-www-form-urlencoded string; or an empty string if the http.queryparamlist object is empty

name: http.response.bodystream
doc: Returns the stream id of the response body. It is not necessary to rewind the stream, the position is already at the start of the data retrieved from the server. In case a stream id was passed using the HTTP_RESPONSE_BODY option, this returns that stream id.
syntax: function long http.response.bodystream (long response)
returns: a stream id

name: http.response.curlcode
doc: Returns the cURL code stored in the response object. A cURL code of 0 means that communication was successful. Any other code indicates that communication was not successful. Reasons may be e.g. that the host could not be resolved, or (in case of https) that there are issues with the certificate(s).
syntax: function long http.response.curlcode (long response)
returns: a cURL code, 0 means OK, any other code indicates an error

name: http.response.delete
doc: Deletes an http.response object. If the response object contains a body stream that was automatically opened, the stream will be closed as well.
syntax: function void http.response.delete (long response)

name: http.response.error_message
doc: Call this to retrieve an error message in case there was an error while sending the request.
syntax: function string http.response.error_message (long response)
returns: an English error message, which can be used for debugging and/or logging

name: http.response.headerlist
doc: Returns the list of HTTP headers received from the server.
syntax: function long http.response.headerlist (long response)
returns: an http.headerlist object

name: http.response.request_method
doc: Returns the HTTP method of the request for which the response was created. The HTTP method and the URL are stored to identify to what request the response object belongs.
syntax: function string http.response.request_method (long response)
returns: the HTTP request method, like "GET", "POST" etc.

name: http.response.request_url
doc: Returns the URL of the request for which the response was created. The HTTP method and the URL are stored to identify to what request the response object belongs.
syntax: function string http.response.request_url (long response)
returns: the request URL

name: http.response.statuscode
doc: Returns the HTTP response statuscode, like 200, 404 or 500, etc.
syntax: function long http.response.statuscode (long response)
returns: an HTTP statuscode

name: http.response.statustext
doc: Returns the HTTP response status text, like "OK" (for 200), "Not Found" (for 404), "Internal Server Error" (for 500), etc.
syntax: function string http.response.statustext (long response)
returns: an HTTP status text

name: http.routeparamlist.add
doc: Adds a name-value route parameter pair to an http.routeparamlist object.
syntax: function void http.routeparamlist.add (long routeparamlist, const string name, const string value)

name: http.routeparamlist.add_list
doc: Adds the contents of another http.routeparamlist to an http.routeparamlist object. If route parameters already exist, they are replaced.
syntax: function void http.routeparamlist.add_list (long routeparamlist, long other_routeparamlist)

name: http.routeparamlist.delete
doc: Deletes an http.routeparamlist object. Any contained name-value route parameters pairs are deleted as well.
syntax: function void http.routeparamlist.delete (long routeparamlist)

name: http.routeparamlist.new
doc: Constructs a new http.routeparamlist object. It is possible to initialize the http.routeparamlist object with name-value route parameter pairs. When the http.routeparamlist object is passed to eg. http.get(), the name and value pairs will be used to fill in route parameters in the url.
syntax: function void http.routeparamlist.new ( ...)

name: http.send
doc: Sends an HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.send (const string method, const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.trace
doc: Sends a TRACE HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.trace (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: Identifier
doc: Identifier

name: import
doc: Import retrieves the value of the specified variable of the parent process. This parent process is not always identified by the variable parent in case of dynamic index switching. When using dynamic index switching, the parent process is sometimes killed and restarted. This causes a different paren…
syntax: function [long] import (string variable_name, ref void value)

name: import.4gl.var
doc: Imports a 'predefined' 4GL variable. Like number.of.marks which is actually a macro.
syntax: function void import.4gl.var (string variable_name, ref void value)

name: ims.clearerr
doc: Resets the error and end-of-byte-array indicator.
syntax: function long ims.clearerr (long bytearray)

name: ims.close
doc: Closes the byte array. This is done automaticallly when you leave your process.
syntax: function long ims.close (long bytearray)

name: ims.eof
doc: Detects if the end of the byte array is reached.
syntax: function long ims.eof (long bytearray)

name: ims.error
doc: Detects if an error has occurred while reading from or writing to the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.error (long bytearray)

name: ims.getc$
doc: Returns the next character from the byte array.
syntax: function string ims.getc$ (long bytearray)
returns: If an empty string is returned, either the end of the string has been reached or an error has occurred.

name: ims.getproperties
doc: Returns the properties of the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.getproperties (long bytearray, ref string buffer [, ref long size])

name: ims.gets
doc: Reads characters from the byte array into a buffer ( line).
syntax: function long ims.gets (ref string line, long size, long bytearray [, long skip.mode] [, long there.was.more])

name: ims.openfba
doc: Opens a Fixed Byte Array (FBA).
syntax: function long ims.openfba (string buffer, long size, string type)

name: ims.openvba
doc: Opens a Variable Byte Array (VBA).
syntax: function long ims.openvba (string type [, long initialSize] [, long increment])

name: ims.putc$
doc: Writes a character to the current position in the byte array.
syntax: function string ims.putc$ (string char, long bytearray)
returns: If no error occurs, the written character is returned. Otherwise, an empty string is returned.

name: ims.puts
doc: Writes a line (and a new-line character) to the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.puts (string line, long bytearray)

name: ims.r.long
doc: Reads a 32-bit value from the byte array. The 4 bytes read from the byte array are interpreted as the 32-bit two’s complement representation of a signed integer value.
syntax: function long ims.r.long (long bytearray)
returns: Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream, or end-of-byte-array reached. Notice that this error value -1 cannot be distinguished from normal value -1. This is problematic, unless it is kno…

name: ims.r.short
doc: Reads a 16-bit value from the byte array. The 2 bytes read from the byte array are interpreted as the 16-bit binary representation of an unsigned integer value.
syntax: function long ims.r.short (long bytearray)

name: ims.r.utc
doc: Reads a specified amount of bytes from the byte array. The bytes read from the byte array are interpreted as the two’s complement representation of a signed integer value.
syntax: function long ims.r.utc (long bytearray [, long byte.count])
returns: Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream, or end-of-byte-array reached. Notice that this error value -1 cannot be distinguished from normal value -1. This is problematic, unless it is kno…

name: ims.read
doc: Reads a number of bytes from the byte array into a buffer.
syntax: function long ims.read (ref string buffer, long nrBytes, long bytearray)

name: ims.rewind
doc: Sets the position in byte array to the beginning.
syntax: function long ims.rewind (long bytearray)

name: ims.seek
doc: Changes the current position within the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.seek (long offset, long opt, long bytearray)

name: ims.setvbaproperties
doc: Sets the properties of the Variable Byte Array (VBA).
syntax: function long ims.setvbaproperties (long bytearray, long increment)

name: ims.skip
doc: Skips forward a number of bytes in the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.skip (long nrbytes, long bytearray)

name: ims.spool.line
doc: Spools a line and writes it to the byte array. The characters in the line are copied to the byte array until the last non-white character in the line is encountered. After that, the contents of the line is cleared.
syntax: function long ims.spool.line (ref string line, long bytearray)

name: ims.tell
doc: Returns the current offset within the byte array relative to the begin of the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.tell (long byetarray)

name: ims.w.long
doc: Writes a 32-bit integer value into the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.w.long (long value, long bytearray)

name: ims.w.short
doc: Writes a 16-bit integer value into the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.w.short (long value, long bytearray)

name: ims.w.utc
doc: Writes an integer value into the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.w.utc (long value, long bytearray [, long byte.count])

name: ims.write
doc: Appends a given number of bytes from the buffer into the byte array, beginning at the current position in the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.write (string buffer, long nrBytes, long bytearray)

name: in.fips.mode
doc: Function to determine whether the bshell runs in FIPS-140-2 compliant mode. This function supports the 3GL/4GL engineer to write FIPS specific compliant code.
syntax: function long in.fips.mode ()

name: inherit.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
syntax: function void inherit.object (long process_nr, long object_id)

name: input.again
doc: After input by a user, this forces the user to input the data again. If there is an input error, it is preferable to use set.input.error() in the check.input subsection for the field.
syntax: function void input.again ()

name: input.to.utc
doc: This converts a string to a local date or local time based on a format.
syntax: function domain ttutc input.to.utc (const string value(), const string format())
returns: The local date or local time value depending on the format string. Or -1 if an error occurs (such as when there is no valid local date or local time value possible for the given string). Related topi…

name: inputfield.invisible
doc: "ttadv301.labl(2)"
syntax: function void inputfield.invisible (string field_name(18),...)

name: inputfield.password
doc: "ttadv301.labl(2)"
syntax: function void inputfield.password (string field_name(18),...)

name: inputfield.visible
doc: "ttadv301.labl(2)"
syntax: function void inputfield.visible (string field_name(18))

name: inputstr.to.date
doc: This converts a date input string to the number of days since 01-01-0001.
syntax: function long inputstr.to.date (string inputstr(.), string format(7))

name: inputstr.to.utc
doc: This converts the specified local date and time input strings to UTC long format.
syntax: function domain ttutc inputstr.to.utc (const string date.inputstr(), string date.format(7), const string time.inputstr(), string time.format(7))

name: insch$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
syntax: function string insch$ (string attr)

name: insertln$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated.
syntax: function string insertln$ (string string_expr)

name: int
doc: The function int() performs explicit double to long type conversion.
syntax: function long int (double x)
returns: The long value resulting from the described explicit double to long type conversion applied to the supplied input value.

name: is.administrator
doc: This checks whether or not the user that is running the bshell has administrator rights on the server that the bshell is running. On UNIX systems, the function returns TRUE if the user has root access to the system. On Windows NT systems, the function returns TRUE if the user belongs to the adminis…
syntax: function boolean is.administrator ()
returns: TRUE user has administrator rights FALSE user does not have administrator rights

name: is.composite.child
doc: This function checks whether the current session is running as a composite child session or not. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode and as a child within a composite session. This function can be called from a 4GL-Session or from a GBF session.
syntax: function boolean is.composite.child ()

name: is.field.invisible
doc: This checks whether a specified field is currently visible or invisible. To specify a particular element of an array field, append the element number (in parentheses) to the field name. For example: "ttadv301.labl(2)".
syntax: function if not is.field.invisible (string field_name(18))
returns: FALSE field is visible TRUE field is invisible

name: is.field.multi.currency
doc: This returns whether a specified field is a multi currency field.
syntax: function boolean is.field.multi.currency (string field_name(18))

name: is.graph.present
doc: This function indicates whether there are active graph defined for this session. This function can be used to determine if additional operations/calculations are needed for a graph.
syntax: function boolean is.graph.present ()

name: is.image.changed
doc: This function can be used to check if an image has been changed onto the image field or the image is changed which is not yet saved or discarded.
syntax: function boolean is.image.changed (string fieldname)

name: is.image.dropped
doc: This function can be used to check if an image has been dropped onto the image field or the image is deleted which is not yet saved or discarded.
syntax: function boolean is.image.dropped (string fieldname)

name: is.internal.session.graphs.active
doc: This function returns whether the graphs are represented by Internal Session Graphs functionality.
syntax: function boolean is.internal.session.graphs.active ()

name: is.landlord.bse
doc: This function returns TRUE if the current BSE is a landlord BSE; FALSE otherwise.
syntax: function boolean is.landlord.bse ()

name: is.mmt.controller
doc: This function checks whether the current session is running as a multi-main table controller session or not. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode or as a controller within a multi-main table session.
syntax: function boolean is.mmt.controller ()

name: is.mmt.satellite
doc: This function checks whether the current session is running as a multi-main table satellite session or not. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode or as a satellite within a multi-main table session.
syntax: function boolean is.mmt.satellite ()

name: is.multi.tenant.enabled
doc: Deprecated. This function is deprecated as the name is confusing and it is actually the same as function is.landlord.bse().
syntax: function boolean is.multi.tenant.enabled ()

name: is.tenant.bse
doc: This function returns TRUE if the current BSE is a tenant BSE; FALSE otherwise.
syntax: function boolean is.tenant.bse ()

name: is.tree.detail.child
doc: This function tells whether the current session is running as part of a Tree-Detail session. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode and as a child within a Tree-Detail session. This function can be called from a 4GL-Session or from a GBF session.
syntax: function boolean is.tree.detail.child ()

name: is.view.field
doc: This function can be used to check whether a field is currently a view field. This is useful when, for example, the view can be personalized and a total line only makes sense with a specific field in the view.
syntax: function boolean is.view.field (const string fieldname)
returns: True if the field is currently a view field

name: is.webpart.session
doc: This function checks whether the current session is running as a primary session in a Workspace WebPart. This function can be useful when a session can be run in different modes.
syntax: function boolean is.webpart.session ()

name: is_kms_encrypted
doc: Determines if an encrypted password is encrypted with the KMS encryption function.
syntax: function boolean is_kms_encrypted (string encrypted_password)

name: isdigit
doc: This function tests whether the supplied string is the textual representation of an integer value.
syntax: function boolean isdigit (string str_expr)
returns: TRUE string contains the textual representation of an integer value FALSE string does not contain the textual representation of an integer value

name: iso.to.date
doc: This converts an ISO 8601 date string to a local date.
syntax: function long iso.to.date (const string iso.date)

name: iso.to.utc
doc: This converts a string, representing a time in ISO 8601 format into a UTC long value.
syntax: function domain ttutc iso.to.utc (const string iso.string)

name: isspace
doc: This tests whether the result of string_expr contains only spaces or is empty.
syntax: function boolean isspace (string str_expr)
returns: TRUE string is empty or contains only spaces FALSE string is not empty and contains characters other than spaces

name: java.destroy.queue
doc: Removes a queue, given the queue id. This will also remove all buckets on that queue!!
syntax: function long java.destroy.queue (long Queue.id)

name: java.execute.static.application.method
doc: Executes a versioned, dynamically loaded, Java method. These Java mehods can also return a (string) value to the 3 GL.
syntax: function long java.execute.static.application.method (long Handle, ref string JavaReturnValue, string class.name, string method.name [, void ...])

name: java.execute.static.method.sync
doc: Executes a Java static method, with no return type, within the JavaVM.
syntax: function long java.execute.static.method.sync (string class.name, string method.name [, void ...])

name: java.get.bucket
doc: Retrieves a bucket from the queue (if available). The message is removed from the queue afterwards.
syntax: function long java.get.bucket (long Queue.id, ref string body, long length [, ref string header])

name: java.install.listener
doc: Installs a listener at the Infor Enterprise Server side. Whenever a message arrives on the queue specified by queue.id, the 3GL process will be notified by an EVT_CHANNEL_EVENT event. For installation of a listener at the Java side, see the Java IQueueListener interface definition.
syntax: function long java.install.listener (long Queue.id [, long become.owner])

name: java.load.application
doc: Load the most recent version of a Java application and return a handle to be used in subsequent operations. A Java virtual machine (JVM) is started when required (or an existing one is used), see Java VM integration - Infor Enterprise Server 3GL for details.
syntax: function long java.load.application (string Application.Name)

name: java.lookup.queue
doc: Checks whether a queue is still valid and, if so, if the queue contains a message. The message is not removed from the queue.
syntax: function long java.lookup.queue (long Queue.id [, ref string header])

name: java.new.queue
doc: Creates a new queue for buckets. Upon return, the new queue.id is returned, or an error code is presented. NOTE: queues are removed automatically if the process that created it (or the process that called java.install.listener(…) on that queue) is finished !! See also the 3GL function java.install.…
syntax: function long java.new.queue ()

name: java.put.bucket
doc: Places a message onto a queue. The message contains a header (of type string) and a body (which can contain any character).
syntax: function long java.put.bucket (long Queue.id, string body, long length [, string header])

name: java.uninstall.listener
doc: Uninstalls a listener at the Infor Enterprise Server side. All buckets on this queue will remain available. The listener can only be uninstalled by the process that installed the listener.
syntax: function long java.uninstall.listener (long Queue.id)

name: java.unload.application
doc: Unloads an application loaded by java.load.application.
syntax: function long java.unload.application (long handle)

name: job.add.field
doc: Save other fields in the jobdata which are not on the form. All form fields are stored in the jobdata.
syntax: function void job.add.field (string fld_name [, long fld_element] [, long fld_type] [, string fld_descr])

name: Json.add
doc: Adds a JSON value at the end of a JSON array.
syntax: function [long] Json.add (long json_array, long json_value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON value which has been added to the JSON array.

name: Json.addBoolean

name: pipe.clearerr
doc: This resets the error and end-of-file indicators on the specified pipe.
syntax: function long pipe.clearerr (long pipe_id)
returns: 0: success -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: pipe.close
doc: This clears any buffers associated with the specified pipe and closes the file. Buffers allocated by the standard input/output system are also cleared. Note that pipe.close() is performed automatically when the process exits.
syntax: function long pipe.close (long pipe_id)
returns: -1: error -2: child process is not allowed to read/write anymore >= 0: exit value of child process (0 is OK)

name: pipe.eof
doc: This checks the end-of-file indicator on the specified pipe. Note that the end-of-file indicator lasts until the pipe is closed, unless you explicitly clear it by calling pipe.clearerr().
syntax: function long pipe.eof (long pipe_id)
returns: <> 0: end-of-file indicator read on specified pipe 0: end-of-file indicator not read

name: pipe.error
doc: This checks the error indicator on the specified pipe to determine whether an error has occurred when reading or writing to the pipe. Note that the error indicator lasts until the pipe is closed, unless you explicitly clear it by calling pipe.clearerr().
syntax: function long pipe.error (long pipe_id)
returns: <> 0: error has occurred when reading or writing to the pipe 0: no error has occurred

name: pipe.flush
doc: This writes any buffered data associated with a pipe to the related file. The stream remains open.
syntax: function long pipe.flush (long pipe_id)
returns: 0: success -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: pipe.gets
doc: This reads a maximum of one line from the specified pipe.
syntax: function long pipe.gets (ref string line, long nr_of_bytes, long pipe_id)
returns: 0: success -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: pipe.open
doc: This creates a UNIX process with the specified name and links an input and/or output stream to it. It returns a pointer to the pipe; this is used to identify the pipe in subsequent operations.
syntax: function long pipe.open (string pathnm, string openmode)
returns: >= 1: success; a pointer to the pipe is returned < 1: error; that is, the negative value of the system error (for example, for a permission error, the system returns 13 and the function returns -13,…

name: pipe.puts
doc: This writes data to the specified pipe. It automatically appends a newline character to the data.
syntax: function long pipe.puts (string line, long pipe_id)
returns: 0: success -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: pipe.read
doc: This reads a specified number of bytes from the specified pipe.
syntax: function long pipe.read (ref string buffer, long nr_of_bytes, long pipe_id)
returns: > 0: the number of bytes read 0: end-of-file -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: pipe.write
doc: This appends a specified number of bytes to the specified pipe.
syntax: function long pipe.write (string buffer, long nr_of_bytes, long pipe_id)
returns: > 0: the number of bytes written 0: end-of-file -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

returns: The number of filled children.

name: rdi.domain.date

returns: 0 success -1 error

name: rdi.domain.set

returns: 0 success -1 error

name: rdi.domain.set.value

returns: 0 success -1 error
